item.title: Over 360 patients waiting over 18 months for treatment at local hospitals
item.description: Over 360 patients are waiting over 18 months for treatment at local hospitals. The most recent report from the National Treatment Purchase Fund reveals just over 5,300 inpatients were on the waiting list as of the end of January. A total of 5,330 are languishing on outpatient waiting lists at Sligo, Roscommon, Portiuncula and Mullingar hospitals. Advertisement As of the 31st of January, this number included 189 children. item.title: Status yellow rain and snow warning for local counties to kick in at midday
item.description: The country is waking up to frost and ice, with the first of a number of weather warnings in place. The entire country is subject to a status yellow low temperature and ice warning until 10am. Temperatures have fallen between minus 1 and minus 3 degrees, leading to hazardous travelling conditions. item.title: Over 30,000 recipients of State Pension Contributory across region
item.description: There are over 30,000 recipients of the State Pension Contributory in the Shannonside Northern Sound region. Figures were revealed earlier this week following a parliamentary question from Deputy Malcom Byrne to Minister for Social Protection, Dara Calleary. The State Pension Contributory is a weekly, non-means-tested payment for people aged 66 or over with sufficient PRSI contributions, payable regardless of other income. item.title: Roscommon senator says apprentices are 'badly needed' in the county
item.description: The Seanad has heard Roscommon is one of only three or four counties in Ireland without an apprenticeship training centre. Castlerea senator Gareth Scahill says the county urgently needs one. He says some people can't get their houses adapted or retrofitted for up to two years because of a lack of tradespeople. Senator Scahill says new apprentices are badly needed given the demand for housing: Advertisement

item.title: Leitrim farmer calls for Larry Murrin to resign as chair of Bord Bia
item.description: A former Leitrim Councillor and farmer says Larry Murrin must resign as the chair of Bord Bia. Sinn Féin last week had proposed a motion calling on Murrin to be removed from his position after it emerged that 1% of the beef his company Dawn Farm Foods used came from Brazil. However, the Government opposed the motion and used its majority to amend it and express support for Mr Murrin in the Dáil. Leitrim farmer John Ward has criticised the Government's handling of the issue: Advertisement

item.title: 'Tears, smiles and even laughter' at funeral of Englishman who died after alleged assault in Ballaghaderreen
item.description: There were 'tears, smiles and even laughter' as the Englishman who died after an alleged assault in Ballaghaderreen was laid to rest. Jorden Newin, 39, suffered serious injuries after the alleged assault in the early hours of New Year’s Day and later died in hospital. The father-of-three's funeral took place in the Garden of England Crematorium in Bobbing in Kent on Thursday. item.title: Only two properties available to let as commercial accommodation in Longford Town
item.description: Only four properties across the Shannonside Northern Sound region are available to rent long-term as commercial accommodation, despite 23 being advertised on Airbnb. Cavan Town and Longford Town are the only areas in the region exempt from new laws that will curb short-term lets. This means that property owners in towns with a population of between 10,000 and 20,000 will no longer be required to get planning permission to provide commercial accommodation. item.title: Offaly TD raises concerns about proposed windfarm in South Roscommon
item.description: An Offaly TD has raised concerns about a proposed windfarm in South Roscommon. The Cornafulla Wind Farm is a joint venture between Bord na Móna and SSE Renewables. Around 200 locals are against the plans - with a group set up called the Friends of Clonmacnoise, Cornafulla and the Shannon Callows. Independent TD Carol Nolan is also against the plans: Advertisement

item.title: Galway and Kerry draw in division one
item.description: Galway came from behind to draw with Kerry in round three of the Allianz League on Saturday evening. Shane McGrath scored a crucial two-pointer late as it finished Galway 3-14 Kerry 2-17. The Kingdom had a 10 point lead in that game with 11 minutes to go. Galway manager Padraig Joyce also confirmed Paul Conroy will play football for Galway this season.
